chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Fazzal, from Ibn Bukayr who said:

I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about the one with sexual impurity eating and drinking and reciting (the Quran). He (peace be upon him) said: 'Yes, he can eat and drink and recite (the Quran), and mention Allah, Mighty and Majestic, whatever he so desires to.'

key_terms.الْجُنُبِ: The one in a state of major ritual impurity (junub)
key_terms.يَقْرَأُ: He recites (typically referring to Quran recitation)

ai.seo_question: Can a person in a state of junub eat, drink, and recite the Quran?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies that major ritual impurity (junub) does not restrict general acts of worship or daily activities, distinguishing it from minor impurity (hadath) which requires wudu. Imam al-Sadiq (AS) explicitly permits eating, drinking, and reciting the Quran, indicating that the prohibition on recitation for the junub is often a matter of scholarly precaution (ihtiyat) rather than a strict divine ban, as the state of junub only necessitates ghusl for prayer and entering the mosque. This ruling underscores the Shia view that ritual purity is primarily linked to specific acts of worship rather than a general state of impurity affecting all bodily functions.
